title: Duplicate orders on double-submit
eyebrow: How the bug happens · order creation

overview.summary: Submitting the same order key twice creates two orders when the second request arrives before the first one commits. The duplicate check reads the store and the insert writes it as two separate steps, so there is a gap where both requests see no order. A slower store widens the gap, so the bug fires more often under load, and retries after a timeout make a second submit likely.

tabs.title: When it fires
tabs.lede: Two things must both be true; slow storage and retries only make them likelier.

factors.name: Second request lands before the first commits

scenarios.label: Second submit after the first commits

etc: Confirmed by sending two requests 10 ms apart against a local store with injected latency.
Not tried: a second submit routed to a different server instance.

tabs.title: How it happens
tabs.lede: The same two requests end in one order or two, depending on who reaches the store first.

steps.what: The second duplicate check runs before the first insert lands.
